newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda, Sudan agree to release prisoners in peace move.
newsitem.headline: Uganda, Sudan agree to release prisoners in peace move.

text.p: The presidents of Uganda and Sudan, at talks arranged by Kenya, have agreed to release all those held captive in border clashes.

The agreement was contained in a formal communique published on Sunday after a meeting between Presidents Yoweri Museveni of Uganda, Omar Hassan al-Bashir of Sudan and Daniel arap Moi of Kenya in the west Kenyan town of Eldoret on Saturday.
Moi invited Museveni and Bashir to the meeting in an attempt to resolve the deep differences between Uganda and Sudan, which accuse each other of helping rebels on their common border.
The communique said Bashir and Museveni also agreed to reactivate past agreements between their countries. Uganda cut diplomatic relations with Sudan in 1995.

The official Kenyan Presidential Press Unit quoted Moi as saying in Eldoret that he hoped Uganda and Sudan would reach an amicable solution to their problems because the region needed development instead of conflict.

Moi said he was calling a meeting of a subcommittee of the Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGAD) to help end civil war in south Sudan. The committee includes representatives of Kenya, Uganda, Eritrea and Ethiopia.

Moi, who first held separate talks with Museveni and then with Lieutenant-General Bashir, said he hoped their meeting on Saturday would be a firm beginning towards trust between the member states of IGAD.
IGAD has in the past helped arrange meetings between the Sudanese goverment and the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), led by Colonel John Garang.

Museveni and Bashir said they "appreciated the positive points" in the Sudanese government's recent peace agreement with southern factions other than the SPLA and agreed that Garang might have a role in solving "other humanitarian problems".
Uganda accuses the Sudanese government of arming and giving bases in south Sudan to Ugandan rebels of the Lord's Resistance Army. Sudan accuses Uganda of arming and supporting the SPLA.

The SPLA has fought since 1983 for greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem, Arabised north and has scored its biggest success since 1991 with a series of offensives this year.
The LRA has been severely weakened by the strength of the SPLA in the south but Garang denies he is fighting for Uganda.
Uganda last month said its army killed 60 Sudanese soldiers and captured more than 100 just inside northern Uganda, beating back a joint attack by the Sudanese army and Ugandan rebels.
It displayed what it said were 114 captured Sudanese soldiers and 16 Ugandan rebels state-run radio said had fled into Uganda to escape attacks by the SPLA in southern Sudan.

At about the same time last month, Sudan displayed several men it said were Ugandan prisoners of war captured after a battle with the Sudanese army in south Sudan. Uganda denies sending its own troops to fight alongside the SPLA rebels.
